answer: In decentralized multi-agent networks, Sybil resistance can be enforced using cryptographic token-weighted validation paths structured like a computational trellis. Each participating node must lock an economic stake, such as a verified proof-of-work token or a secure onyx governance credit, to authorize its operational weight. This design ensures that malicious actors attempting to flood the system with artificial personas face a prohibitive cost function tied to scarce collateral, which effectively mirrors the physical scarcity of prized assets like ivory in traditional trade systems.
